1. A residential colony under the name and style of Brahma City was launched by M/s. Brahma City Pvt. Ltd. (formerly known as M/s. Brahma Krrish Buildtech Pvt. Ltd. and M/s. Krrish Buildtech Pvt.
Ltd. (in short accused company), through its Director Amit Katyal in Sector - 60, 61, 62, 63 and 65,
Gurugram, Haryana, in the year 2010 - 2011.

The company claimed to have obtained License No. 64 of 2010 dated 21/08/2010 from Department of Town & Country Planning (DTCP), Govt. of Haryana, to develop land ad-measuring 151.569 acres into residential colony.

2. Accused company entered into contract with multiple buyers and obtained booking amount from them in consideration of development of land and sale of plots to them in aforementioned residential colony.
The accused company undertook to execute Sale Deed and to handover the possession of land to the buyers within 03 years of entering into agreement.

sentences.text: When the accused company failed to develop the land and to handover the possession of plots to the buyers, they filed separate criminal complaints with allegation that the accused company, its Directors and other co-accused persons cheated them of money by falsely representing that they had license to develop the land under sale.

There were allegations by multiple buyers that accused persons wrongfully reduced the contracted plot size and also changed the plot numbers after obtaining substantial part of the sale consideration amount.
Several complainants also alleged that the accused persons wrongfully obtained booking amount in respect of same plot number from different buyers.
4. The FIR of this case was registered on 07/03/2019 at PS EOW for offence U/s. 409/420/120B IPC.
The criminal complaints received from plot buyers against accused persons in respect of aforementioned project were clubbed in present case and were investigation together as one single case.

61, 62, 63 and 65, Gurugram, Haryana.

He argued that in pursuance of invesment agreement dated 03/06/2010 executed between Aman Katyal and Brahma Opportunities Ltd. (BOL), whereby BOL subscribed to 74% share holding of KBPL and balanced share holding of 26% was held by M/s.
Krrish Infracture Pvt. Ltd. (KIPL) and Amit Katyal.

On 16/12/2010, the name of Krrish Buildtech Pvt. Ltd. was changed to M/s. Brahma Krrish Buildtech Pvt. Ltd.
10.

It is argued that the aforementioned project faced several challenges and hardships, whereby initially its land area under License No. 64 (supra) was reduced from 151.569 acres to 147.281 acres by DTCP as it was discovered by DTCP that land measuring 4.2875 acres was inadvertently included in the said license.

Subsequently, revised layout plans of the licensed land had to be submitted by accused company to DTCP in view of over head high tension wires and Indian Oil Corporation gas pipeline running through the licensed land.

11. It is argued that one M/s. Fondant Propbuild filed writ petition (CW) P. No. 27665/2013 before Hon'ble High Court of Punjab & Haryana for quashing of License No. 64 (supra) granted to the accused company in view of wrongful inclusion of land belonging to it in the aforementioned license.

In the said case, Hon'ble High Court of Punjab & Haryana, through order dated 17/12/2013,
directed to maintain status quo on the entire land.
Because of this reason, the development of land faced legal road block.

Subsequently, DTCP, through letter dated 08/05/2015 provisionally approved the revised demarcation plan-cum-layout plan subject to further directions of Hon'ble High Court of Punjab & Haryana in aforementioned writ petition.
Through final order dated 05/02/2015 Hon'ble High Court of Punjab & Haryana quashed License No. 64 (supra) and remanded back the matter to DTCP for reconsideration.

DTCP considered the application of accused company and directed it to fulfill certain requirements before restoration of license for area measuring 141.781 acres for the residential township.

The accused company complied with directions of DTCP,
whereupon DTCP restored License No. 64 (supra) in its favour and also, in principle, approved revised layout plan - demarcation plan and invited objects and suggestions from existing allottees.
13.

It is argued that, after considering the objections and suggestions of the allottees and others,
DTCP approved the layout-cum-demarcation plan on 02/11/2016 and zoning plan on 07/07/2017 in an area of 141.668 acres under License No. 64 (supra) granted to accused company.
14. The charge-sheet filed by IO is voluminous and is a jumble of allegations and counter-claims from both sides.

It is apparent from charge-sheet that FIR was got registered by the complainants primarily because of delay in development of residential colony and non-execution of sale deed of booked plots in favour of buyers by the accused despite lapse of considerable time after stipulated period of 03 years.

15. The relevant questions in reference to the allegations of cheating are - (i) Whether the revisionist company had intention to cheat the customers of their money while entering into agreements with them for development and sale of plots in question?
(ii). Whether every aspect of designing and development of the residential project was final and within control of the accused?
(iii). Whether accused deliberately stalled the construction/ plotting of the project in order to delay or refuse to execute sale of plots in favour of buyers?

(iv). Whether the land proposed to be developed was government land, disputed land or there was litigation related to ownership of the land?
(v). Is there any evidence in charge-sheet that accused contracted to sell more plots constituting the land than was available with it for sale?
In this regard, it is essential to peruse the agreements executed between the parties while obtaining booking amount from customers.

At the time of execution of agreements between the parties pertaining to booking of plots, it was open land of around 140- 150 acres on which development of plots to be sold was proposed.

The buyers could not be heard arguing that they did not even know that plotting would be contingent upon several factors including clearance of demarcation and layout plans by DTCP, environmental clearance by government etc.

Apart from delay caused in finalization of demarcation and layout plan by DTCP, delay caused in obtaining environmental clearance, delay caused due to cancellation/suspension of licence and subsequent restoration thereof by DTCP and delay occasioned due to Court orders, there is nothing in charge-sheet to suggest that accused deliberately delayed the project and intended to avoid the plotting and execution of sale of plots in favour of buyers.

16.

The charge-sheet reflects that M/s. Brahma City Pvt. Ltd. obtained environmental clearance from State Environment Impact Assessment Authority, Haryana, Panchkula, through Letter No.
SEIAA/HR/2014/1143 dated 03/09/2014 in respect of the land in question.

sentences.text: The obtaining of environmental clearance for developing and plotting the land is a reflection on bona fide intention of the accused to develop the land.
17. The accused obtained Licence No. 64 (supra) in respect of private land partly owned by them and partly in collaboration with third parties.

The charge-sheet does not mention that there was any litigation pertaining to ownership of the land sought to be developed by accused or any litigation pertaining to authority of the accused to develop and offer it for sale to buyers.

18. It is observed that every breach of contract would not give rise to an offence of cheating and only in those cases breach of contract would amount to cheating where there was any deception played at the very inception.
If the intention to cheat has developed later on, the same cannot amount to cheating.
For the purpose of constituting an offence of cheating, the complainant is required to show that the accused had fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of making promise or representation.

Even in a case where allegations are made in regard to failure on the part of the accused to keep his promise, in the absence of a culpable intention at the time of making initial promise being absent, no offence under Section 420 IPC can be said to have been made out.

It is true that a given set of facts may make out a civil wrong as also a criminal offence and only because a civil remedy may be available to the complainant that itself cannot be a ground to quash a criminal proceeding.

The real test is whether the allegations in the complaint disclose the criminal offence of cheating or not [Ref.: Vesa Holding Private Limited & Anr. Vs. State of Kerala & Ors.
(2015) 8 SCC 293].

In the present case there is nothing to show that at the very inception there was any intention on behalf of the accused persons to cheat which is a condition precedent for an offence under Section 420 IPC.
19.
The charge-sheet does not mention about discovery of any evidence that accused contracted to sell more plots constituting the land than was available with it for sale.

The allegations pertaining to subsequent act of accused in offering lesser than agreed / booked plot area to some of the buyers and in offering the same plot number to more than one buyer would be considered in reference to the aforementioned written agreement that in the event of change in layout plans, the plot number,
its location as well as size offered to buyer may also be changed.
In view of contingency disclosed in the agreement, the aforementioned subsequent act of accused would not come within purview of offence of cheating right from the beginning.

The seller i.e. the accused is under contractual obligation to execute the sale documents in respect of plot of size commensurate to the consideration amount received from the buyer, however, the buyer could not claim the right to a specific location or specific serial number of plot, in view of contingency involved in development of residential colony.

Similarly, in the situation in present case, in which the delay occasioned because of circumstances beyond control of the accused,
the buyers could scarcely allege that they were cheated by the accused.
Things would have been different if the agreement between the parties pertained to an already developed residential colony with plots of specific size and serial numbers.
Then there would be no contingency involved and seller would be under strict obligation to sell the contracted plot to the buyer.

20. At this juncture, it is reiterated that in order to constitute an offence of cheating, the accused must have intention to deceive right from the beginning when agreement was executed; a mere failure to keep the promise subsequently or to strictly adhere to terms of contract would not convert dispute between the parties into an offence of cheating.

Thereafter, vide office order dated 02.12.2015, the licence No. 64/2010 for the area 141.66875 acres was restored by the DTCP in compliance of the orders dated 05.02.2015 of the Honble Punjab and Haryana in CWP No. 27665 of 2013.

sentences.text: Apart from bare allegations of buyers, who were exasperated by delay in plotting and handing over of possession of booked plots, there is nothing in charge-sheet to justify the invocation of offence U/s. 420 IPC r/w Section 120B IPC against the accused.
The charge-sheet was filed simply on the basis of contents of complaints filed by buyers whilst overlooking the explanation and counter-claim received from the accused.
There was no independent investigation into the allegations made by buyers.
The Court cannot act as an agent or mouthpiece of police and it is under solemn obligation to independently apply its mind to charge-sheet, without borrowing opinion of the IO.
The cognizance of an offence can and should be declined if, on perusal of material collected during course of investigation, the offence does not appear to have been committed by the accused.

23. The impugned order reflects that Ld. Trial Court did not independently apply its mind to the charge-sheet and simply borrowed opinion of IO that there was sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused for offence U/s. 420 IPC r/w Section 120B IPC, for which they should be put to trial.
To this extent, the impugned order was unjust and unreasonable and is hereby set aside.
The cognizance for offence U/s. 420 IPC r/w Section 120B IPC is liable to be declined.

24. So far as offence U/s. offence U/s. 409 IPC r/w Section 120B IPC is concerned, it is applicable only in cases in which accused being in any manner entrusted with property or with any dominion over property and acted in capacity of a public servant or in the way of his business as a banker,
merchant, factor, broker, attorney or agent.
In present case, the accused acted in none of the capacity as mentioned above.
The accused obtained booking amount from buyers towards part consideration of sale of proposed plots.
There was relationship of seller and buyer between them and entrustment of money with accused in that limited capacity.

25. The impugned order reflects that Ld. Trial Court did not independently apply its mind to the charge-sheet and simply borrowed opinion of IO that there was sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused for offence U/s. 409 IPC r/w Section 120B IPC, for which they should be put to trial.
To this extent, the impugned order was erroneous and unreasonable and is hereby set aside.
The cognizance for offence U/s. 409 IPC r/w Section 120B IPC is liable to be declined.

Subsequent act of the accused - Criminal Breach of Trust :
26.

As per charge-sheet, in pursuance of their criminal conspiracy, accused have diverted the money received from buyers / complainant and meant for plotting purposes to other accounts; thereby they misappropriated the money to their personal benefit in contravention of contractual obligations.
The accused have not accounted for the money entrusted to them by buyers for plotting purposes.
27. On the basis of charge-sheet, there is sufficient reason to proceed against accused for offence U/s. 406 IPC r/w Section 120B IPC.
Ld. Trial Court shall proceed with cognizance of offence U/s. 406 IPC r/w Section 120B IPC against all the accused.
With these observations and directions, the revision petition is hereby disposed of.
TCR be sent back to Ld. Trial Court alongwith copy of this order, for information and compliance.
